body.statement: For the unequal six-block population with \(r=(1,1,1,3,3,3)\), \(n=12\), and \(\alpha=1/4\), the three size-three coordinates cap and the three size-one coordinates do not. Explicitly, \(\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{24(\log4-3/8)}\), \(\omega_{1/4}=3/4+\sqrt{(\log4-3/8)/24}\approx0.9553\), and the subset retaining only size-one blocks gives \(\rho_0\le3/4+1/\sqrt{24}\approx0.9541\).
body.justification: The numerical exhibit exposes the cap threshold and the near-matching trimming certificate in a reproducible unequal-block instance.
body.gap: An equal-block substitution has only one breakpoint and therefore cannot reproduce simultaneous capped and uncapped coordinates.
body.consumer: The software diagnostic uses this instance as a unit test for sorting, multiplier solution, and trimming output.
body.proof_tex:
For a size-one block, \((w_l,q_l)=(1/12,1/2)\), so \(q_l/w_l=6\); for a size-three block, \((w_l,q_l)=(1/4,1/8)\), so \(q_l/w_l=1/2\).  If the three size-three coordinates cap and the other three do not, the active constraint is
\[
 {3\over8}+3\cdot{1\over2}\left({\lambda_\alpha\over6}\right)^2
 ={3\over8}+{\lambda_\alpha^2\over24}=\log4.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{24(\log4-3/8)}\).  Numerically \(1/2<\lambda_\alpha<6\), verifying the proposed cap pattern against both breakpoints.  The objective at this certified optimizer is
\[
 3\cdot{1\over4}+3\cdot{1\over12}{\lambda_\alpha\over6}
 ={3\over4}+\sqrt{{\log4-3/8\over24}}\approx0.9553.
\]
For \(\rho_0\), retain the three size-one blocks and omit the other three.  The corresponding value is
\[
 {3\over4}+\sqrt{3{(1/12)^2\over1/2}}={3\over4}+{1\over\sqrt{24}}\approx0.9541,
\]
which proves the stated upper certificate.
